items.title: China’s Spies Set Sights on A.I. Chips Years Before Nvidia Scandal
items.excerpt: China’s espionage agency has been running a secret campaign to help the country’s companies acquire advanced A.I. chips and to gather intelligence on the sector, officials say.

items.title: Canada’s Boreal Forest Is Reshaped by Logging and Climate Change
items.excerpt: Canada has framed the preservation of its boreal forest as a model for the world, but commercial logging combined with climate change is inflicting severe damage.

items.title: Drones, Texts and Diversions: How Mexico Captured a Most Wanted Man
items.excerpt: U.S. and Mexican authorities shared intelligence for weeks to track Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, a drug cartel leader that a U.S. official called the most dangerous man in Mexico.

items.title: South Korea’s Education Minister Resigns Over Anti-A.I. Cheating Rules
items.excerpt: Two days before South Korea’s college entrance exam, new measures were announced, including loud phone alerts and eyeglass inspections. Public backlash came fast.

items.title: Taiwanese Comedian Targeted for Mocking Xi Jinping Is Drawing Sellout Crowds
items.excerpt: “Xi Jinping is my comedy muse,” said Huang Yi-hao, who survived a car crash the authorities say was meant to silence him.

items.title: Deadly Protests Erupt in Bangladesh Over Exiled Former Leader. What to Know.
items.excerpt: Supporters of the deposed prime minister, Sheikh Hasina, who was sentenced to death in absentia, have waged a small-scale insurgency to destabilize the current government.

items.title: Top Drug Kingpin Is Captured by Mexican Army as Gunfire Erupts
items.excerpt: The arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, who is known as El Chapo Isidro and was one of the F.B.I.’s 10 most wanted, was a victory for the Mexican government.

items.title: Catherine, Princess of Wales, Documents Life With Cancer in BBC Film
items.excerpt: “Cancer does change you,” Catherine, who is in remission, says in a trailer for the film. It will be released this month.

items.title: Pentagon Issued Memo Limiting ‘Social Activities’ With Canadian Military
items.excerpt: The latest salvo in the fraught U.S. relationship with Canada has not affected their vast joint military operation, including the shared airspace command, NORAD.

items.title: Who Is the Mexican Drug Kingpin Known as El Chapo Isidro?
items.excerpt: The kingpin, Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, was captured in a violent operation in Mexico. He was one of the F.B.I.’s 10 most wanted fugitives.

items.title: Victims of Clerical Sexual Abuse Want More Engagement From Pope Leo
items.excerpt: As he toured South America this month, Pope Leo XIV met with 11 victims of clerical sexual abuse. Some want him to engage more meaningfully.

items.title: U.N. Fails to Regulate Lethal Autonomous Weapons, but Plans to Try Again
items.excerpt: Major military powers like the United States and Russia expressed strong resistance to binding restrictions.

items.title: On the Trail With Spain’s Prime Minister, as He Tries to Pull Out a Win
items.excerpt: Pedro Sánchez, Europe’s most prominent left-wing leader, seems set to lose power in an election next week. Our reporter trailed his last-ditch effort to turn his campaign around.

items.title: In France’s Angry Autumn, TV News Channels Are Accused of Stirring the Pot
items.excerpt: Critics say that CNews and BFM TV, two major news channels, have used racist language in protest coverage. The channels deny it.

items.title: Israeli Political Leaders Denounce ‘Jewish Terrorism’ After West Bank Attacks
items.excerpt: Extremist settlers carried out a spate of violent raids in Palestinian villages over the weekend, spurring opponents of the Netanyahu government to demand a forceful response.

items.title: Is Mexico Stepping Up in the War on Drugs?
items.excerpt: With several powerful drug kingpins recently taken down by Mexican forces, some experts see what may be a new chapter beginning in Mexico.

items.title: A Landmark Genocide Ruling
items.excerpt: A U.N. court’s decision against Myanmar sets a precedent in international law with important implications for a similar case over Israel’s actions in Gaza.

items.title: How Melania Trump Found a Diplomatic Opening in the War in Ukraine
items.excerpt: The first lady, who has little experience in international affairs, developed back channels to key figures on both sides of the conflict through her longtime agent.

items.title: COP31 Talks Collapse in Turkey in a Clash Over Fossil Fuels
items.excerpt: European and vulnerable nations rejected a proposed agreement after Saudi Arabia and other oil producers blocked any mention of phasing out coal, oil and gas.

items.title: American vs. Chinese Mahjong: Why the Rivalry Is Stirring Controversy
items.excerpt: American mahjong, with its own tiles and rules, has overshadowed the traditional Chinese game. The rivalry has fueled anger and cultural misunderstanding.

items.title: A Chinese Tech Hub Offers a Peek at the Electric Cars Headed for Canada
items.excerpt: Prime Minister Mark Carney attended an economic summit in the city of Shenzhen, where electric vehicles rule the hectic, but largely silent, road.

items.title: Maldon Salt’s Authenticity Is Questioned, Leaving Foodies Shaken
items.excerpt: The salt is a flaky favorite of food influencers and famous chefs. A revelation this week raised questions about what makes artisanal “artisanal.”

items.title: A Butler School in the Netherlands Offers Entry Into a Gilded World
items.excerpt: An academy in the Netherlands offers an eight-week, $14,000 program for entry into a gilded world of service. What’s the appeal?

items.title: White Police Officers Are Convicted of Beating a Black Man in France
items.excerpt: The three officers were filmed beating Michel Zecler, a music producer, inside his Paris studio in 2020, setting off a national backlash.

items.title: Denmark Expels Russian Diplomat After Accusing Moscow of Planning a Hit
items.excerpt: Danish officials say Russian intelligence services recruited members of a violent gang to try to assassinate a Ukrainian rapper at a concert outside Copenhagen.

items.title: Chinese-Born Neuroscientist Is Detained by ICE While Traveling From Conference
items.excerpt: Eva Yi Xie was detained on her way back to New Jersey from a neuroscience conference in Washington this week, the latest in a string of researcher arrests.

items.title: Britain and Brussels Have Begun a Brexit Rollback. How Far Will It Go?
items.excerpt: The United Kingdom is removing barriers with the European Union a decade after it voted to leave. Global turmoil, and the disruptive policies of President Trump, helped push them back together.

items.title: Devilish or Delightful? Krampus Is Banned From a Christmas Parade.
items.excerpt: After an appearance last year, a float depicting Krampus, St. Nicholas’s evil accomplice, will not be allowed in an Ontario town’s Santa Claus parade on Saturday.

items.title: Iraqi Forces Enter Stronghold of Powerful Iran-Backed Militia
items.excerpt: For the first time in over a decade, army and police units were deployed in territory controlled by the group, Kataib Hezbollah. But it was unclear if it would withdraw its forces.

items.title: ‘Russian Objects’ Crashed in Poland, Officials Say. Here’s What We Can See.
items.excerpt: There were no injuries or damage from three incidents that the Polish authorities called a likely “provocation” from Russia during military exercises by Ukraine’s allies.
